Front Load Washer Drain Pump Replacement

Written By: Repair Volunteer
  • Comments2

Difficulty

Moderate

Steps

13

Time Required

1 - 2 hours

Introduction

If your front-loading washing machine leaves water in the drum at the end of a cycle, or hums without draining, the drain pump may be blocked or burnt out.

This guide shows how to clear the pump filter first, and then how to replace the pump if clearing it does not help. It is written for the common European-style machines with a filter door at the bottom front.

Tools

  • Phillips #2 Screwdriver

  • Flathead Screwdriver

  • Pliers

  • Towels

  • Shallow tray

Parts

  • Drain pump (check the model number on the old pump)

  1. Step 1

    • Unplug the washing machine from the mains and turn off the water taps before you start. Never work on a washer that is plugged in: water and mains electricity together can kill.

    • Wait until the water in the drum has cooled if a hot cycle was running.

  2. Step 2

    • Lay towels on the floor in front of the machine and put a shallow tray under the filter door.

    • A washer can hold several litres of water even when it looks empty, so have a bucket ready to empty the tray.

  3. Step 3

    • Open the small filter door at the bottom right of the front panel with a flathead screwdriver.

    • Pull out the short emergency drain hose, remove its cap and let the water run into the tray.

    • Close the cap each time the tray is full and empty it.

  4. Step 4

    • When no more water comes out, turn the filter knob anticlockwise and pull it out.

    • Remove coins, hair clips, lint and any other debris from the filter and from the opening behind it.

    • Turn the pump impeller with a finger through the opening. It should turn in jerks and then spin freely; if it does not move at all, the pump is jammed or seized.

    Found a sock in mine, the whole thing was full.

    Reader 41 - 4/04/2021

    On my Bosch the impeller has a bit of play, that is normal.

    Reader 42 - 5/05/2021

  5. Step 5

    • Refit the filter, plug the machine in and run a drain or spin cycle.

    • If it now drains, you are done. If it still does not drain and the pump hums, continue to replace the pump.

  6. Step 6

    • Unplug the machine again.

    • Tilt the washer back against a wall and prop it up securely, or lay it on its side on a blanket if the pump is reached from below.

    • A washer weighs 60 to 80 kg; get a helper and keep your fingers clear.

    Tip: lay it on its LEFT side, the motor side is heavier and less likely to spill.

    Reader 43 - 6/06/2021

  7. Step 7

    • Remove the screws holding the kick plate or the bottom panel under the front of the machine.

  8. Step 8

    • Locate the drain pump behind the filter housing.

    • Take a photo of the hoses and wires so you can put them back the same way.

  9. Step 9

    • Loosen the hose clamps with pliers and pull the hoses off the pump.

    • More water will run out of the hoses; keep the towels in place.

  10. Step 10

    • Disconnect the two wires from the pump by pulling the connector, not the wires.

  11. Step 11

    • Remove the screws holding the pump to the frame, often three Phillips screws, and pull the pump free.

    • Compare the new pump with the old one: the connector, the outlets and the mounting holes must match.

  12. Step 12

    • Fit the new pump, screw it in, reconnect the wires and slide the hoses back on.

    • Tighten the hose clamps so that they sit over the ridges of the outlets.

  13. Step 13

    • Stand the machine up, plug it in and run a rinse and spin cycle.

    • Check under the machine with a torch for drips during the cycle.

    • If water leaks from the filter door, the filter was not turned in all the way.

Written By: Repair Volunteer

Difficulty

Easy

Steps

9

Time Required

15 - 30 minutes

Introduction

A worn chain shifts badly, skips under load and wears out the cassette and chainrings. Replacing it in time is cheap; waiting can mean buying a new cassette as well.

This guide covers derailleur bikes with 8, 9, 10 or 11 speeds.

Tools

  • Chain checker

  • Chain tool

  • Master link pliers

  • Rag

Parts

  • Bicycle chain (same speed count as your drivetrain)

  • Master link

  1. Step 1

    • Measure the chain with a chain checker.

    • Replace it when it shows 0.5 percent wear on an 11-speed chain, or 0.75 percent on 8 to 10 speeds.

    • Without a checker, measure 12 links with a ruler: a new chain measures exactly 12 inches (304.8 mm) from pin to pin; replace it at 12 1/16 inches.

    My shop says 0.5 for all of them now.

    Reader 47 - 10/01/2021

    Ruler trick works great!

    Reader 48 - 11/02/2021

  2. Step 2

    • Shift to the smallest rear cog and the smallest front chainring.

    • This leaves the most slack in the chain.

  3. Step 3

    • Find the master link, a link with a different shape or colour, and squeeze it with master link pliers to open it.

    • If there is no master link, push out any pin with the chain tool.

  4. Step 4

    • Pull the old chain off the bike.

  5. Step 5

    • Size the new chain: wrap it around the largest front ring and the largest rear cog without going through the derailleur, pull it tight, and add two links (one inch).

    • A chain that is too short can rip the derailleur off the frame when you shift to the largest cogs.

  6. Step 6

    • Break the new chain at that length with the chain tool.

  7. Step 7

    • Thread the new chain through the front derailleur, over the cassette and through the rear derailleur pulleys.

    • Follow the path of the old chain; it should not touch the tabs of the derailleur cage.

  8. Step 8

    • Join the ends with the new master link.

    • Turn the pedals so that the link is on the top run, hold the rear brake and push down hard on a pedal to snap the link closed.

Ceiling Fan Capacitor Replacement

Written By: Repair Volunteer

Difficulty

Moderate

Steps

10

Time Required

30 - 60 minutes

pages.wikipedia_en_all_maxi_2026-01/Transforme:
Transformer

A transformer is a passive electrical device that transfers electrical energy from one circuit to another by electromagnetic induction.[49] It is used to raise or lower the voltage of alternating current.

A step-up transformer raises the voltage and a step-down transformer lowers it; power grids use both, so that power can travel far at high voltage and be used safely at low voltage.

Principles

[edit]

An alternating current in the primary winding makes a changing magnetic flux in the core, and the flux induces a voltage in the secondary winding.

The ratio of the voltages equals the ratio of the numbers of turns: a transformer with 1,000 turns on the primary and 50 on the secondary steps 230 V down to 11.5 V.

Ideal transformer

[edit]

In an ideal transformer no energy is lost, so the current changes in the opposite ratio to the voltage: stepping the voltage down by ten times steps the current up by ten times.

Construction

[edit]

Core

[edit]

The core of a power transformer is made of thin sheets of silicon steel, stacked and insulated from each other to cut the eddy currents that would heat it.[50]

Small transformers for high frequencies use cores of ferrite, a ceramic made of iron oxide mixed with other metals.

Some transformers for audio have no iron core at all.

Windings

[edit]

The windings are usually made of copper wire coated with enamel, or of aluminium in large units to save cost.

The winding with more turns has the higher voltage and uses thinner wire, because it carries less current.

Cooling

[edit]

Large transformers are filled with mineral oil, which insulates the windings and carries heat to radiators.

The oil can burn, so substations keep transformers apart behind fire walls.

Types

[edit]

A step-down transformer in a phone charger or a doorbell lowers mains voltage to a few volts.

An autotransformer has a single winding with a tap, and it is smaller but does not isolate the two circuits.

An isolation transformer has a 1:1 ratio and is used to separate equipment from the mains for safety.

Current transformers let meters measure large currents safely.

Efficiency

[edit]

Large power transformers are over 99 percent efficient; small ones lose more in their copper and core.

Safety

[edit]

Transformers connected to the mains carry dangerous voltages; never open a transformer that is connected, and remember that a step-up transformer's secondary can be far more dangerous than the mains itself.

History

[edit]

Michael Faraday showed induction between two coils in 1831.

The first practical transformers for power systems were built in Hungary in 1884 and 1885.

pages.wikipedia_en_all_maxi_2026-01/Stepper_mo:
Stepper motor

A stepper motor is a brushless electric motor that divides a full turn into a number of equal steps.[51] Its position can be commanded to move and hold at one of these steps without a sensor, as long as the motor is not overloaded.

Stepper motors are used in 3D printers, CNC machines, camera lenses and many other devices that need precise positioning.

Fundamentals of operation

[edit]

The rotor carries permanent magnets or soft iron teeth, and the stator has coils that are switched on in sequence to pull the rotor round one step at a time.

The most common hybrid stepper motors make 200 steps per revolution, so each full step is 1.8 degrees.

Types

[edit]

Permanent magnet steppers often have 7.5 or 15 degrees per step and are cheap.

Hybrid steppers combine a magnet with toothed iron and give finer steps and more torque.

Driving

[edit]

A driver circuit turns each coil on and off in order; each pulse from the controller moves the motor one step.

In half-stepping the driver alternates between one and two coils, doubling the number of steps to 400 per turn.

Microstepping divides each full step into as many as 256 smaller steps by varying the current, for smoother motion.

The first step in wiring a stepper motor is to find the two coils: the two wires of a coil show low resistance between them.

Problems

[edit]

If the load is too great, or the steps come too fast, the motor misses steps and loses its position without knowing it.

Stepper motors get hot even when standing still, because current flows to hold the position.

Applications

[edit]

A desktop 3D printer usually has four or five stepper motors of the NEMA 17 size, which has a face plate of 1.7 inches.

Pachelbel's Canon

Pachelbel's Canon is a piece of music by the German Baroque composer Johann Pachelbel, written for three violins and basso continuo and paired with a gigue in the same key.[52]

Its composition is usually dated between 1680 and 1706, but no manuscript from Pachelbel's lifetime survives, and the circumstances of its composition are unknown.

Composition

[edit]

The canon is in D major. Over a bass line of eight notes repeated 28 times, the three violins play the same melody, each entering two bars after the one before.

The composition consists of 28 variations of the melody over the repeated bass, growing from long notes to quick runs and back.

It may have been composed for the wedding of Johann Christoph Bach in 1694, at which Pachelbel was a guest, but there is no proof.

Rediscovery

[edit]

The piece was nearly forgotten until it was published in 1919, and it became widely known only after a recording by Jean-François Paillard's orchestra in 1968.

Influence

[edit]

The chord sequence of the canon, often heard in pop songs, is called the Pachelbel progression.

It is one of the most often played pieces at weddings.

Cookbook:Chapati

Chapati is an unleavened flatbread of India, Pakistan and East Africa, cooked on a dry griddle and eaten with curries, stews and beans.

CategoryBread recipes
Servings8 chapatis
Time1 hour

Ingredients

[edit]
  • 2 cups (250 g) whole-wheat flour
  • 1 teaspoon salt
  • about 3/4 cup (180 ml) warm water
  • 2 tablespoons oil, plus more for cooking

Equipment

[edit]
  • Large bowl
  • Rolling pin
  • Flat griddle or heavy frying pan

Procedure

[edit]
  1. Mix the flour and salt in a bowl, then add the oil and rub it in with your fingers.
  2. Add the warm water a little at a time, stirring, until a soft dough forms that does not stick to your hands.
  3. Knead the dough on a floured surface for 8 to 10 minutes until it is smooth and springy.
  4. Cover the dough and let it rest for at least 30 minutes; this makes the chapatis softer.
  5. Divide the dough into eight balls and roll each one into a thin circle about 18 cm across.
  6. Heat the griddle over medium-high heat until a drop of water sizzles on it.
  7. Cook each chapati for about 30 seconds until bubbles appear, turn it, brush with a little oil and cook until brown spots form.
  8. Stack the cooked chapatis in a cloth to keep them soft and warm.

Notes, tips, and variations

[edit]
  • For flaky East African chapatis, roll the dough out, brush it with oil, roll it up like a rope, coil it and roll it out again.
  • If the chapatis are hard, the dough was too dry or they were cooked too long on low heat.

Bicycle Maintenance and Repair/Tires/Puncture repair

A puncture in an inner tube can be repaired with a patch kit at the roadside in about fifteen minutes. A kit holds patches, vulcanising solution, a piece of sandpaper and usually tyre levers.

Procedure

[edit]

Step 1: Remove the wheel from the bicycle. On a rear wheel, shift to the smallest cog first so the chain comes away easily.

Step 2: Let out any remaining air and push the valve up into the tyre. Hook a tyre lever under the bead opposite the valve and lever it over the rim; hook the second lever two spokes along and run it around the rim.

Step 3: Pull out the tube. Pump some air into it and listen or feel for the hole; if you cannot find it, hold the tube under water and look for bubbles.

Step 4: Roughen the area around the hole with the sandpaper, a little bigger than the patch. Spread a thin layer of vulcanising solution over it and wait until it looks dry, about five minutes; this is the step people most often rush.

Step 5: Press the patch firmly onto the solution and hold it for a minute. Leave the backing on if it is clear plastic.

Step 6: Before putting the tube back, run your fingers carefully around the inside of the tyre to find the thorn or glass that caused the puncture, or it will puncture again.

Step 7: Put a little air in the tube, fit it into the tyre starting at the valve, and push the bead back onto the rim with your thumbs. Do not use the levers to refit the tyre, as they can pinch the tube.

Step 8: Pump the tyre to the pressure printed on its side.

Tips

[edit]

A step-through frame makes it easier to remove the rear wheel on some city bikes.

Carry a spare tube on long rides; patching can wait until you get home.

Making water safe: boiling and disinfection

Water from rivers, wells, rain tanks and broken pipes can carry germs that cause diarrhoea, cholera and typhoid. Boiling is the surest way to kill them; chemical disinfection is the next best.

Boiling

Bring the water to a full rolling boil for one minute. Above 2,000 metres, boil for three minutes, because water boils at a lower temperature there.

Let the water cool in the covered pot and store it in a clean container with a lid. Boiling does not remove chemicals or salt.

Cloudy water

If the water is cloudy, let it settle and pour the clear water off, or filter it through a clean cloth, before boiling or disinfecting it.

Household bleach

Use only plain unscented bleach without added cleaners, and read the label for its strength. Follow the dose on the label or from your local health authority, and wait at least 30 minutes before drinking.

The water should smell slightly of chlorine; if it does not, repeat the dose and wait another 15 minutes.

Things to carry

  • Pot with a lid

    For boiling and for keeping the water covered while it cools.

  • Clean containers

    With narrow necks or taps, so that hands and cups do not go into the water.

  • Cloth filter

    A folded cotton cloth removes much of the dirt and some of the germs from cloudy water.

Comments

Is it true that bleach water must stand overnight? My neighbour says so.

We use a ceramic filter at the clinic and then add chlorine.

Annapurna Circuit trek

The Annapurna Circuit is a trek of 160 to 230 km around the Annapurna massif in central Nepal, crossing the Thorong La pass at 5,416 m. Most people take 12 to 18 days.

Understand

The trek climbs through rice terraces and forest to dry high valleys like those of Tibet. A road now covers parts of the old trail, and many trekkers take a jeep on those parts.

Permits

Trekkers need an Annapurna Conservation Area Permit and a TIMS card, sold in Kathmandu and Pokhara. Since 2023 a licensed guide is required for foreign trekkers in this area.

Get in

Buses run from Kathmandu to Besisahar, the usual start, in about six to eight hours. Jeeps continue to Chame.

Sleep

Teahouses, simple lodges run by local families, line the whole route. A room often costs little or nothing if you eat your meals there.

Eat

Dal bhat, rice with lentil soup and vegetables, is served everywhere and refilled for free. Prices rise with the altitude because food is carried up by porters and mules.

Stay safe

Altitude sickness is the main danger. Above 3,000 m, do not sleep more than 300 to 500 m higher than the night before, and add a rest day every 1,000 m.

If headache, vomiting, confusion or breathlessness at rest appear, go down at once; do not cross the pass with symptoms.

The pass can be closed by snow from December to March, and trekkers have died in sudden storms. Check the weather in Manang before crossing.

Buy

There are ATMs in Besisahar, Chame and Jomsom, but they often run out of money; carry enough Nepali rupees in cash for the whole trek.

Homemade ginger beer

by the kitchen team

This ginger beer is made with fresh ginger, sugar, lemon and a little yeast, and it is ready to drink in two or three days.

Ingredients

  • 100 g fresh ginger, grated
  • 200 g sugar
  • juice of two lemons
  • 1/4 teaspoon dried yeast
  • 2 litres water

Method

  1. Boil the ginger and sugar in one litre of water for five minutes, then add the rest of the water cold.
  2. When the liquid is lukewarm, stir in the lemon juice and the yeast.
  3. Pour into clean plastic bottles, leaving a hand’s width of space at the top, and close them.
  4. Leave at room temperature for one to two days, squeezing the bottles each day; when they are hard, move them to the fridge.

Safety

Glass bottles can burst from the pressure of the gas; use plastic bottles, and open them slowly over the sink.

The drink holds a little alcohol, usually under one percent, so it is not suitable for people who must avoid alcohol completely.

How to patch a bicycle inner tube

A patched tube is as good as a new one if the glue is left to dry before the patch goes on. You need a patch kit, two tyre levers and a pump.

Instructions

  1. Step 1

    Take the wheel off the bike and let all the air out of the tube.

  2. Step 2

    Lever one side of the tyre off the rim with two tyre levers, then pull the tube out.

  3. Step 3

    Pump a little air into the tube and find the hole by listening, or by holding the tube in a bowl of water.

  4. Step 4

    Sand the area and spread the glue thinly; wait until it is dry to the touch, about five minutes.

  5. Step 5

    Press the patch on hard for a full minute.

  6. Step 6

    Feel inside the tyre for the thorn, refit the tube and pump it up.

Tips

  • Carry a spare tube on long rides and patch the punctured one at home, where you can take your time with the glue.
  • A tube with a cut longer than a fingernail, or a hole next to the valve, cannot be patched well; replace the tube.
  • Self-adhesive patches are quicker but come off more often than glued patches, especially on tubes that run at high pressure.
  • Check the tube for a second hole before refitting it: a pinch flat from a pothole often makes two holes side by side, like a snake bite.
  • Keep the patch kit in a bag, because the glue tube dries out once it has been opened, even with the cap on.

Troubleshooting

If the tube goes flat again within a day, the patch may be lifting at its edge: peel it, clean the tube and patch it again with fresh glue.

If a new tube goes flat in the same place, the cause is in the tyre or the rim: a thorn still in the tyre, a sharp spoke end or a torn rim tape.

Gunpowder

Gunpowder, also called black powder, is the earliest known chemical explosive. It burns very quickly and gives off a large volume of hot gas, which can push a bullet out of a gun or lift a firework.

History

[edit]

Chinese alchemists made the first gunpowder in the ninth century while looking for a medicine for long life.

Fire arrows and bombs made with it were used in Chinese wars by the eleventh century.

Knowledge of it reached the Islamic world and Europe in the thirteenth century, and the first guns were made soon after.

Early cannons were made of bronze or wrought iron hoops.

Composition

[edit]

In its standard form, gunpowder is a mixture of about 75 percent potassium nitrate (saltpetre), 15 percent charcoal and 10 percent sulfur by weight.[54]

The saltpetre gives the oxygen, the charcoal is the fuel and the sulfur makes it light more easily.

Manufacture

[edit]

The ingredients were ground together while wet to avoid sparks, pressed into cakes and broken into grains of the size wanted.

Grains made larger burn more slowly, which suits big guns; fine grains are made for small arms and priming.

Uses

[edit]

Black powder was replaced in guns by smokeless powders in the 1880s, but it is still made for fireworks, fuses and muzzle-loading guns.

Quarries once used it to split stone, because it pushes rather than shatters.

Safety

[edit]

Gunpowder can be set off by a spark, by friction or by static electricity, and it should not be made at home; many people have been badly burnt or killed doing so.
